v1.description: Base ReAct prompt: WORLD CONTEXT, PLANNING PHASE order, BOOKING RULE, THOUGHT DISCIPLINE, LETHAL SCENARIOS
v1.notes: Initial implementation. Do not use for new runs — regresses planning quality vs v2.

v2.description: Default prompt: v1 + explicit constraint-tracking guidance + ITINERARY STATE section + cancel_booking instruction
v2.notes: Standard for all training runs. Default in react_default.yaml.

v3.description: v2 + strict format requirement with inline example + error-recovery + real-time budget tracking
v3.notes: Better format compliance. Added after format failures and budget overruns in v2 runs.

v4.description: v3 + CONTEXT SECTION GUIDE to reduce agent confusion between compressed-state sections
v4.notes: Experimental. Use when agents confuse HARD_CONSTRAINT_LEDGER with DECISIONS_MADE.

v5.description: v4 + STEP-BUDGET PHASED PLANNING with hard deadlines per phase
v5.notes: Current default for Colab training runs. Reduces deadline-missing failures.

sweep_A.description: Grow-then-Prune strategy: build a candidate itinerary then prune to meet budget/constraints
sweep_A.notes: Standalone prompt-design experiment. Not derived from v-series.

sweep_B.description: Ordered pipeline with per-category booking quotas

sweep_C.description: Commit-every-step: search-book pairs must alternate strictly

sweep_D.description: Minimal Viable First: book minimum viable itinerary (1 flight + 1 hotel + 1 activity) before enhancing
sweep_D.notes: Confirmed non-degenerate in 11 steps during baseline prompt sweep. Recommended for COMPRESSOR baseline.

sweep_E.description: Step-budget phased planning with explicit phase deadlines

sweep_F.description: Stateless agent: no trajectory history, itinerary-only memory (STATELESS mode)
sweep_F.notes: Requires agent.mode=stateless. Cannot be used with COMPRESSOR or MCTS_COMPRESSOR.

sweep_G.description: Commitment gate: every action must advance the booking state or exit
sweep_G.notes: Requires agent.mode=stateless. Cannot be used with COMPRESSOR or MCTS_COMPRESSOR.
